text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The number of small companies which are trying for listings on the stock exchange is growing as entreprenuers race to secure capital for investments.
- Swedish commercial bank Handelsbanken must pay 12 million crowns to a former female employee at the bank's New York office for alleged sex discrimination, a New York court rules.

- Peggy Bruzelius, the new vice managing director of S-E-Banken, says in an interview she is not especially good at remembering figures and advises women who want to be managers to pay for household help instead of trying to do everything themselves.
- The price of zinc has risen 26 percent in one year. For metals and mining group Trelleborg's Boliden unit, this means a profit increase of 300 million crowns on an annual basis.

- Interest from Swedish shareholders falls when companies move operations abroad. Since Dutch Akzo bought Nobel Industrier three years ago, four of five Swedish shareholders have left the company. Before Swedish drug company Pharmacia merged with U.S. rival Upjohn, some 86 percent of Pharmacia shareholders were Swedish. This figure has fallen to 23 percent since the merger.
